summary: Describes GMPLS control for Provider Backbone Bridge Traffic Engineering (PBB-TE), including the extensions to set up Ethernet point-to-point and point-to-multipoint connections.

eli5.summary: This lets a GMPLS control system set up fixed Ethernet paths across a carrier backbone, as well as branching paths.

questions: control ethernet backbone traffic engineering with gmpls
how does gmpls control ethernet paths
what is an ethernet switched path
what is the pbb-te ethernet label
subtitle: How GMPLS signaling can set up fixed, pre-planned Ethernet paths across a carrier backbone.

tldr.problem: IEEE PBB-TE lets a provider build explicitly routed Ethernet paths by configuring static forwarding entries in bridges, but it needs something to set those entries up bridge by bridge.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC uses GMPLS and RSVP-TE for this. A new Ethernet label carries a VLAN ID and a MAC address, a new switching type marks the path as PBB-TE, and a Service ID TLV can tie a service instance (I-SID) to the path.
tldr.outcome: A GMPLS control plane can create, maintain, protect and tear down PBB-TE paths while the standard IEEE data plane stays unchanged.

today: RFC 6060 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the framework in RFC 5828.

sections.title: Why PBB-TE Needs a Control Plane
sections.content:
IEEE 802.1 Provider Backbone Bridge Traffic Engineering (PBB-TE) supports explicitly routed, traffic engineered paths inside Provider Backbone Bridged networks. For administratively selected VLAN Identifiers it allows the Spanning Tree Protocol, unknown destination address forwarding and source address learning to be disabled.

Paths are then built from static entries in the bridges' managed objects, configured by an external provisioning system or a control plane. This RFC specifies the extensions that let a GMPLS (Generalized MPLS, RFC 3945) control plane do that job. It complements the GMPLS Ethernet Label Switching Architecture and Framework in RFC 5828, and it supports but does not modify the standard IEEE data plane.
sections.eli5: Normally Ethernet switches figure out where to send things by watching traffic. PBB-TE turns that off and uses fixed routes, and this RFC says how a controller can write those routes into the switches.

sections.title: Paths, Services and Terminology
sections.content:
An Ethernet Switched Path (ESP) is a provisioned, unidirectional path between Customer Backbone Ports (CBPs). It is identified by the 3-tuple <ESP-MAC DA, ESP-MAC SA, ESP-VID>. A point-to-point ESP joins two CBPs. A point-to-multipoint ESP has one root and n leaves, and its destination address is a group MAC address. An ESP set up by GMPLS is called an Ethernet-LSP (Eth-LSP).

A point-to-point PBB-TE Service Instance (TESI) is two co-routed point-to-point ESPs between the same CBP MAC addresses, forming a bidirectional service. A GMPLS bidirectional LSP is therefore analogous to a P2P TESI.

ESPs always start and end on IB-Backbone Edge Bridges (IB-BEBs), which contain an I-component and a B-component. The I-component adds the I-SID and a MAC header with ESP-MAC DA and SA, and the B-component adds the ESP-VID. In the GMPLS control plane, TE Router IDs identify IB-BEBs and Backbone Core Bridges, and TE Links describe links to PNPs and CNPs. TE Links are not associated with CBPs or PIPs.
sections.eli5: An ESP is a one-way road from one door of the network to another. Two matching one-way roads make a two-way street, which is what a service needs.

sections.title: Setting Up a Point-to-Point Eth-LSP
sections.content:
Forwarding uses only the ESP-MAC DA and the ESP-VID in each direction. With GMPLS, those two values are carried in a generalized label object and assigned hop by hop, but they stay the same across the domain. Each PBB-TE Ethernet Label is therefore domain-wide unique for each direction.

To start a bidirectional Eth-LSP, the initiator follows RFC 3473 and:

  • MUST set the LSP encoding type to Ethernet (2) and the switching type to 802_1 PBB-TE (40);
  • SHOULD set the G-PID to Ethernet (33);
  • MUST set UPSTREAM_LABEL to the ESP-VID1/ESP-MAC1 tuple for its own MAC address;
  • SHOULD use LABEL_SET or SUGGESTED_LABEL to influence the choice;
  • MAY carry an I-SID via Call/Connection ID.

Intermediate bridges MUST NOT modify label values. Each hop installs a static forwarding entry from the label and the port derived from the RSVP_HOP object. At the destination, ESP-VID2 is allocated for MAC2 and returned in the LABEL object of the RESV message, which is installed the same way. Because PATH and RESV follow the same path, the result is a bidirectional Eth-LSP. If UPSTREAM_LABEL is left out, RSVP-TE can set up a unidirectional ESP.

Make-before-break can modify a P2P Eth-LSP as described in RFC 3209, and signaling can be combined with protection switching so that only the protection path is modified.
sections.eli5: The sender suggests a route label on the way out, the receiver picks one for the way back, and every switch in between copies the labels into its own table without changing them. Now both directions are planned.

sections.title: Labels, Shared Forwarding and P2MP
sections.content:
The PBB-TE Ethernet Label is a new generalized label: four zero bits, a 12-bit ESP VID, and a 48-bit ESP MAC. It MUST be used for both P2P and P2MP Eth-LSPs, carrying a unicast MAC for P2P and a group MAC for P2MP, and it MUST be passed unchanged at each hop. The RFC compares this to a wavelength label at a bridge that cannot convert wavelengths. The RFC lists the label as 60 bits and the full ESP 3-tuple as 108 bits.

Shared forwarding MAY be used to reuse one destination forwarding entry (common ESP-VID and ESP-MAC DA, unique ESP-MAC SA) for several sources. It is a local decision based on label allocation and path constraints, it does not change the paths themselves, and it can reduce the number of forwarding entries. Resources can still be allocated per LSP. A Path Computation Element or planning tool can pre-select shared labels using LABEL_SET and UPSTREAM_LABEL.

VLAN priority bits MAY indicate class of service and drop priority, so traffic from several classes can share one Eth-LSP.

For P2MP, the procedures of RFC 3473 and RFC 4875 could be adapted for the root-to-leaves direction, with each branch paired with a reverse-path P2P Eth-LSP. Complete procedures for bidirectional P2MP are out of scope.
sections.eli5: The label is a short address tag made of a lane number and a mailbox address. Several senders heading to the same place can share one signpost, which saves space in the switches.

sections.title: Protection and Service Identification
sections.content:
When protection is used, working and protection paths are put into a protection group with the ASSOCIATION and PROTECTION objects defined in RFC 4872 and RFC 4873.

The I-SID uniquely identifies a service, so it should be unique across the network or at least between any pair of edge bridges. On an IB-BEB the Backbone Service Instance Table maps I-SIDs to ESPs, either by manual configuration or semi-automatically through signaling. Signaling the I-SID also helps the IB-BEB pick the right CBP.

Two carriers are defined. CALL signaling (RFC 4974) MAY create an association before the LSP exists, using the new Service ID TLV in the CALL_ATTRIBUTES object. Alternatively the PATH message can carry the TLV in LSP_ATTRIBUTES (RFC 5420), at setup or later through a PATH refresh. The TLV holds one or more I-SID Set Objects, each either a list (0) or a range (1) of 24-bit I-SIDs.
sections.eli5: A service gets a ticket number called an I-SID. The signaling can tell both ends which ticket goes with which road, so nobody has to type it in by hand.

sections.title: Error Conditions
sections.content:
Operators pick the set of VLAN IDs usable for ESPs, and every bridge should be configured with the same range. A VID outside the range is invalid. If a bridge is not configured to use the ESP-VID in the label, it MUST immediately generate Routing problem (24) / Unacceptable label value (6), and the error is handled as in RFC 3209. It travels in a PathErr, or in a ResvErr if the problem shows up on the RESV message.

If the allocated VID range is used up, the destination bridge SHOULD send a PathErr with Routing problem (24) and value MPLS Label allocation failure (9).

MAC addresses 01-80-C2-00-00-00 to 01-80-C2-00-00-0F are reserved by IEEE and cannot be used for ESPs. A label that refers to one makes the bridge generate the same Unacceptable label value error.
sections.eli5: If a switch is told to use a lane number or address it is not allowed to use, it immediately says no and tells the sender why.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says it introduces no new security issues; the considerations in RFC 4872 and RFC 4873 apply. It assumes that users and devices at UNIs may behave maliciously, negligently or incorrectly, while intra-provider control traffic is trusted. With in-band signaling, control-plane and data-plane security affect each other; out-of-band signaling decouples them.

Where control links use 802.1AE MAC Security, no further measures may be needed. Otherwise control-plane security is appropriate where deemed necessary, using the GMPLS and RSVP-TE techniques of RFC 3471, RFC 3473, RFC 3209 and RFC 2205, with a fuller overview in RFC 5920.
sections.eli5: Strangers at the edge might misbehave, so the inside of the network only trusts messages from its own controllers, and it can lock them with extra security if it needs to.
